body:
With your recurring grassroots support now we can have the resources we need to take this movement all the way to the U.S. Senate.
# [](https://act.hillharper.com/go/130?refcode=em20231103&t=1&akid=528%2E62735%2ETxIEcu)
Peter, here’s the thing: **for a campaign like ours, time is of the essence.**
Here’s what we mean by that:
1️⃣ **$5 now makes more of an impact on our campaign than $50 right before the election.** That’s because the earlier we build a strong foundation of resources, the more we’re able to get out into the community, organize, reach voters, and volunteers and make a difference when it comes to election day. Odds are, folks who just find out who Hill Harper is the day before election day aren’t going to be voting for him at the ballot.
2️⃣ **A steady stream of donations month after month that we can depend on helps us plan ahead.** One of the hardest parts of being a grassroots campaign is the unpredictability of fundraising. One month we can surpass our fundraising goals, other months we can fall short. That takes a toll on how far in advance we can plan events, and travel. If we don’t know how much money we’ll have on hand we may have to cut critical initiatives and change plans.
**That’s why one of the most powerful ways you can support our effort is by making a recurring donation of any amount.** It will go a long way in helping us be sure that we’re able to run a strong, statewide campaign that reaches _as many people as possible_.

clean_body: The Clinton-Qatar-Hamas Connection [WEEKLY UPDATE] BEST OF: SPEAKER JOHNSON MUST RELEASE THE JAN 6 TAPES! [] THE CLINTONS, QATAR, AND THE ISRAEL MASSACRE It’s not easy to understand the Middle East, but one facet can be found in following the money. One open-wallet nation, Qatar, has been chummy [] with both Hamas terrorists and U.S. politicians. Our chief investigative reporter Micah Morrison provides the details [] in our Investigative Bulletin about Qatar’s connections with a former U.S. president and a secretary of state. Shortly after the world began learning the details of the massacre of Israeli civilians on October 7, Hillary Clinton published a note of support [] on X for “everyone affected by the horrific attacks by Hamas” and expressed “strong support of our ally,” Israel. The former secretary of state had nothing to say about one of Hamas’s key allies, the energy-rich kingdom of Qatar, and not surprisingly: Qatar is not only an important friend of the U.S. in the region but also for many years was a generous patron of Bill and Hillary Clinton. As Judicial Watch President Tom Fitton noted on X [], Qatar funneled money to the Clintons when Mrs. Clinton was secretary of state and she “hid this until disclosures from Wikileaks and pressure from Judicial Watch forced her to admit to tens of millions of previously hidden foreign cash payments to ‘Clinton Inc.’” Slipping money into the hands of slippery politicians—a time-honored tradition in the Middle East and elsewhere—of course is not the same as providing significant ongoing state support for a murderous terrorist organization. But the Clinton experience does provide a snapshot of the Qatari influence operation and a warning about what Qatar may be up to elsewhere, including in the United States. The Qatar-Clinton money trail begins around 2008, when the Clinton Foundation—under pressure due to Mrs. Clinton’s imminent ascent to State Department leadership—published a list of donors. Among them: Qatar, listed as contributing between $1 million and $5 million. A Clinton Foundation spokesman later acknowledged that Qatar had been sending the Clintons money “since 2002.” Pressure mounted on the Clintons in 2014 with the publication of a Judicial Watch investigative report [] disclosing that Bill Clinton had earned upward of $48 million in speaking fees around the globe, including from Arab countries, while Mrs. Clinton served as secretary of state. “Former President Clinton trotted the globe collecting huge speaking fees while his wife presided over U.S. foreign policy,” Tom Fitton noted at the time. In 2016, a leaked Wikileaks email [] revealed that five years earlier, in 2011, the Clintons had received a $1 million gift from Qatar. That gift was never reported by the Clintons, a clear violation of the disclosure agreement the Clintons had signed with the State Department when Mrs. Clinton took the helm. Soon after the 2011 gift, a high-ranking Qatari official pressed the Clinton circle for “five minutes” with the former president. Judicial Watch Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) lawsuits also turned up more evidence of Clinton conflicts of interest, [] including the courting of Qatar. A Judicial Watch FOIA disclosure in late 2016 revealed a list sent by a Clinton Foundation senior adviser to a high-ranking aide to Secretary of State Clinton; the list [] noted more than 200 foreign leaders to be invited to the 2009 Clinton Global Initiative annual meeting, including the emir of Qatar, the Qatari prime minister, and the minister of foreign affairs. Qatar’s pursuit of influence in the United States is not limited to the Clintons and their allies. According to investigative reports [], Qatar has given $1 billion to American universities since 2011. Qatar also is a major purveyor of anti-Semitism. Its media is filled with anti-Semitic and anti-Israel propaganda []. And at the UN—not exactly a bastion of pro-Israel sentiment—a high-ranking Qatari official was recently denied a senior post on the grounds of anti-Semitism []. That’s useful context when considering Qatar’s role supporting Hamas. Here at Judicial Watch, we’re watching Qatar closely. At home, with concern rising about anti-Semitism on U.S. campuses, we won a recent lawsuit forcing disclosure of information about Qatar’s funding of American universities []. Abroad, with lessons learned from our Clinton investigations, we’re following the flow of Qatari money. We’ll keep you updated. TALIBAN CREATES FAKE NONPROFITS TO GET MILLIONS IN U.S. AFGHANISTAN AID It may shock you to know that millions of your tax dollars are being given to the Taliban in Afghanistan. Our Corruption Chronicles blog explains []. In one of the most recent Afghanistan debacles, the Taliban has established fraudulent non-governmental organizations (NGO) to loot the hundreds of millions of dollars in humanitarian aid that the United States has sent Afghanistan since the 2021 military withdrawal. NGOs are typically nonprofits with humanitarian missions that supposedly work to improve public or social welfare. Approximately 1.5 million [] NGOs operate in the U.S., according to the State Department, and they advocate for a variety of issues that include the environment, healthcare, women’s rights, marginalized populations, youth empowerment and economic development. The U.S. government gives NGOs billions of taxpayers every year through various agencies, including the departments of Health and Human Services, Homeland Security and State. In Afghanistan terrorists are not surprisingly stealing the humanitarian aid that keeps flowing to the central Asian Islamic nation by, among other things, utilizing fake NGOs. Specifically, the Taliban is benefiting from American education funding through the establishment of fraudulent NGOs to receive donor assistance, according to an audit [] published recently by the Special Inspector General for Afghanistan Reconstruction (SIGAR). The Taliban is also infiltrating and extorting existing Afghan NGOs delivering educational assistance, the probe found. “For example, an NGO official told us the Taliban are targeting and extorting Afghans who receive monetary support from U.S.-funded education programs under the guise of taxation,” the report states. “In another example, NGO officials told SIGAR that the Taliban are coercing NGOs to hire Taliban supporters or purchase goods from Taliban-owned companies.” Prior to the Biden administration’s abrupt military withdrawal, the U.S. invested $1.3 billion on education-related programming in Afghanistan and reportedly it “contributed to significant improvements” in the Muslim nation’s education system. Since the terrorist group returned to power in August 2021, Uncle Sam has continued to fund Afghanistan’s education sector through six programs that cost $185.2 million even though the Taliban has issued decrees drastically limiting access to education for girls and women as well as restricting women’s ability to work and other basic freedoms. Nevertheless, the American taxpayer dollars keep flowing. In fiscal year 2023, which ended in September, the U.S. sent Taliban-ruled Afghanistan over $566 million [] in humanitarian assistance. Most of it was for emergency food but a chunk was classified as going to general humanitarian and health. More than $15 million went to a cause that is labeled “redacted” in the government records. It’s not like American government officials don’t know the Taliban is taking the money. A report issued earlier this year by the United States Institute of Peace [], the federal institution founded by Congress to promote worldwide conflict resolution, concluded that foreign-funded assistance is unlikely to prove effective as leverage to shape the Taliban government’s behavior. “On the contrary, the Taliban are likely to increasingly regard foreign funded activities as just another potential revenue stream,” the U.S. Institute of Peace found. “Any form of humanitarian or development assistance is prone to manipulation by the Taliban. Aid/development delivery...exposes [foreign donors] to Taliban coercion with little leverage or recourse to resist.” Specific to education, SIGAR writes that the Taliban’s “repressive” policies, especially those targeting girls and women, have severely limited access to, and the quality of, education at all levels. Yet the American taxpayer dollars keep pouring into the terrorist group’s coffers. Laughably, the Islamic Emirate Afghanistan (IEA) denied in a Pakistani news report [] that the Taliban is stealing U.S. education funds, insisting that the IEA acts in the best interest of Afghanistan. “The claims made by SIGAR regarding Afghanistan are far from reality,” according to the IEA’s deputy spokesman quoted in the article. “The Islamic Emirate makes all decisions and manages affairs in Afghanistan based on its principles and the nation’s welfare.” Until next week, [Contribute] [] [32x32x1] [] [32x32x2] [] [32x32x3] [] [32x32x3] [] Judicial Watch, Inc. 425 3rd St Sw Ste 800 Washington, DC 20024 202.646.5172 © 2017 - 2023, All Rights Reserved Manage Email Subscriptions [] |

| | It’s a new dawn and a new day under the leadership of our newly minted speaker of the House, Mike Johnson. But I’m still the same old me: a down-home Tennesseean demanding fiscal responsibility in our nation’s capital. Our friends in Israel are under attack, and I believe with my whole heart that it’s our duty to help them. Yes, this is our ally in the Middle East, and they desperately need us right now, but it’s also simply the _right thing to do._ That’s why I voted to approve[ $14.3 billion in federal aid dollars to Israel](http://links.burchettforcongress.com/u/click?_t=feefb5ad83f24ba4b99ac997c1b47e86&_m=6cf122b6bcd24b5cba21e5858064f67b&_e=PBRZSU65U0J_U4Ux9Zdw4cqUd5kT_rPT7-IY-FNBTMJ-CGMjv5IAwGZL_f1ohiv2kqMoKofySHAE4NUqexvthqOtSLL4A6Ba9wsVcTjdVFTgHgF1mNlLTtGr6qI_H5HekYeFQGlEOYpsftYkqJ7yrM6axaKK9oM_EHT4yf5Qf3K52k8CzS1hWIwybhYtJ5MisiO9GwVCS1jeqpSeRWbfrMArKiKSpd_sGkadE-S4LeVXbDIxI9Yw1aRG-9T-TfhXTsxNJR1CrjDM4xEFrWSxW5dWuaquPPcxW8esUPEroxA%3D). But Speaker Johnson has a fresh take on how to do things from here on out, and because I know we’re on the same page here, I think you’re going to like it. It’s a simple mathematical approach of making cuts in order to make room for spending. Where’s the money for Israel coming from? We’re redirecting cash that was intended for the IRS in President Biden’s useless [Inflation Reduction Act](http://links.burchettforcongress.com/u/click?_t=feefb5ad83f24ba4b99ac997c1b47e86&_m=6cf122b6bcd24b5cba21e5858064f67b&_e=PBRZSU65U0J_U4Ux9Zdw4djr3fUR1pHebk3JtYjiU_IPvMnmhLtDlhbBHKEzI1pvP3QSsWd_pjsG9n1hGMjUUuYD1hVyCnT1B7-8ndcG0w4nKSvddOkumk0MHvIsOrzKi6ykKHd67eheE4cEIVfHqTsu26L26xx4U6LBRrSCZ595NJKiOAaUTuECkPlD-PpXQP6lkRe879IHb1ozP_F3MusItBU2VGRT_QSx5DuTdTgebPHGUtcsueaAZ_WOLhb4MsebLdO8ZpV47uEgD5Y7kVyQqDC0G_nJO-9yy-qRt1o%3D). _ _ In a very on-brand and unsurprising move for Biden, he’s threatening to [veto the bill](http://links.burchettforcongress.com/u/click?_t=feefb5ad83f24ba4b99ac997c1b47e86&_m=6cf122b6bcd24b5cba21e5858064f67b&_e=PBRZSU65U0J_U4Ux9Zdw4V4du4gtqXbRuuBOaQPUFlO1QQ5nhrrY7TQPrOu-WkM50Czoi05tU8aW82t4VHlHEan1XTDXhrnhrKB4Fyll34vT5_dbUTp2bX3PGCO9hO2Sf2_-qCNWiq1om8ePfx2b7xVfXOjKUq6zrqcy31LtPgfAI6-cRb1NJrkH5ck8gBLP5H9OI9fWGqwDhw5bkDmR399RkG9qD-cPIW1l5mXNQD_290AE2B1mfAGcMROGgIfAGdacirvMe0JCjLVga4xBItOnW5BxjnsWczsZOQLNCJ1_OLuH_fFfycy6szHN_Yqm). Democrats want to pull the wool over our eyes and pass an [“aid package”](http://links.burchettforcongress.com/u/click?_t=feefb5ad83f24ba4b99ac997c1b47e86&_m=6cf122b6bcd24b5cba21e5858064f67b&_e=PBRZSU65U0J_U4Ux9Zdw4ZsuUurwJ5lyVbLAWZwt3Vjg-mMVhXtHWkj2I1NvKMDnm9jAtKgQhYnbjP4wRMAxT-ny8Q3TfXA7kArB9jclUfeu8UN6SQH3iQEFhM53m_NG2btqC2BCB3DaHfIplM2Bq7k9rII6NSywtzKFIc7H-hUbZJigCYWTIjaHKMYBZbmDEdzS-vp-7C05e2TwKUDaIEDTnuDUjc77Tt1Wwu-ej6uAOfLecHKi92tMInRtg1SaGQhU0AjT1LLD83kWaXzjGMkMeiEUlC_pLhv4HfKcNQxLDhPkbSWhMJ1Hp0dhoePO) that is lumped in with a whole lot of crud. From more unchecked dollars for Ukraine to border “security,” which is a complete joke when you consider the fact that our southern border is anything but secure, it’s always the same old song and dance with the Left. We are surely headed for a [political showdown](http://links.burchettforcongress.com/u/click?_t=feefb5ad83f24ba4b99ac997c1b47e86&_m=6cf122b6bcd24b5cba21e5858064f67b&_e=PBRZSU65U0J_U4Ux9Zdw4Ra3o7XfSXisN9Z7ewapnwjvpC_ty03EDQDI_fl4rrTHGxeGDRkBhQxaVPEfFLkfygxMhO1TwAWdztKkiirmXxl_Nkg9QjEhluJZNu_XlTTDtCKtI7pdXac9c6hrxaU2rw4QUXN7WsSRReKTBqcGl8TnXxbK1ajAX87g1fwYw8dqkaNM_af3lvqR7-Tgfqz1yZdUtLt7Y_X_IOCH6QaUIghxouOYrKsSo9PdxquyrWXGunQApKcc6w1w08BhAdtSUg%3D%3D) when this thing goes to the Democrat-led Senate. They claim they need IRS funding to go after “tax cheats,” but we know their plan is more swampy than that. They want to [nickel and dime](http://links.burchettforcongress.com/u/click?_t=feefb5ad83f24ba4b99ac997c1b47e86&_m=6cf122b6bcd24b5cba21e5858064f67b&_e=PBRZSU65U0J_U4Ux9Zdw4aONmXz5K7zqivSyFp-jyZtHiyC72p8sgTQtMjjBs3EBY3aKovghDbx-G0EK_EI6vXJ0l2Bq65xCSo6lva--DHFK0d4LzkJA5JO392EJ3k9li1qbQP2DKqysjU_7Tbn2rencyA4rI3PFnchp0JT4Q9Sf-Qos5Dg_TOVrnorti01uOvV2I5COOs3zMo2AfecozBu_x8CSOPMUZ0H8gyi7G6JIk8h1NOFbk9oxNHg17dpKOITm-zF68hBHFxt-qiyfDfl8GOn4zYY6pfOfx7yxkFU%3D) everyday Americans selling something for $600 on eBay. As the old saying goes, Liberals want to rob Peter to pay Paul, and I’ve seen enough. I'm hopeful that we're heading in the right direction with the new speaker on our side, and you can bet your bottom dollar that I'll keep holding the line and demand dadgum responsible budgeting every step of the way.

# Speaker Johnson's first week PLUS Israel, DeSantis and AI...
Speaker Johnson hit the ground running this week. He presented a plan for appropriations, an Israeli aid package balanced against IRS and raised $1 million in fundraising during his first week. In the episode below, I’m joined by Amber Duke and Chris Prather to discuss it all. We break down the conflict in Israel, including horrifying messages from within our country, the Biden administration's response and how they are perceived around the world. Even scarier than Halloween, Vice President Kamala Harris is leading the way on AI and AI safety. And... Is Governor Ron DeSantis wearing heel lifts?

From hosting their first primary debate in Milwaukee to implementing a new GOP early vote program, they could win next November. We can’t let that happen, folks.

That’s why the WisDems and the GA Dems start this work early. **Every cycle since 2017, WisDems uses the one-year-out moment to knock doors, update our data, energize our volunteers statewide, and find the new voters we’ll need to win the following November.**

We call this One Year to Win — a WisDems tradition. But it takes a lot of resources to make something like this successful and our grassroots funds are starting to run low.

Our work over the next month could provide the margin of victory for 2024, which is what makes One Year To Win so important.

_If we don’t hit our fundraising goals, we’d have to significantly cut our capacity at this critical time and sacrifice that margin of victory._

body:
Wanted to share my thoughts with you.

Hi Peter - yesterday the U.S. House, under the leadership of our new Republican Speaker Mike Johnson, passed a bipartisan, single-issue, and fully paid-for $14.2 billion bill to aid our ally Israel in their war against Hamas.

I support this commonsense legislation ... even though President Biden has recklessly threatened to veto it and Senate Democrats are threatening to kill it.

I posted a video last night explaining why. Click here to watch it. (https://secure.anedot.com/max-ukropina-for-congress-2024/bf0ef0a9-11ee-489c-a57b-32f708bc5486?utm_medium=Email&utm_source=Ukropina&utm_campaign=Israel_Aid_113&utm_source=Max+for+OC+Supporters&utm_campaign=fa2c36367c-EMAIL_CAMPAIGN_2023_10_24_03_09_COPY_01&utm_medium=email&utm_term=0_-f436e3f042-%5BLIST_EMAIL_ID%5D)

Israel is one of our oldest and most reliable allies. They absolutely have a right to defend themselves against the terrorist atrocities committed by Hamas. If they are asking for our immediate help, we should provide it to them.

However, I believe that all bills going forward must meet two conditions:
* First, it must be passed as a single-issue bill, instead of being lumped into a massive omnibus with other spending bills that no one has time to read.

* Second, it must be paid for. We cannot afford to go further into debt.

Speaker Johnson's bill accomplishes both of those things.

It only covers one issue - Israel - and it's paid for by cutting funding from the IRS in Biden's Inflation Reduction Act (which does nothing to reduce inflation).

We'll see what the Senate does. But for now, we need to change how Washington works. Single issue, budget-neutral bills like this are a good start. (https://secure.anedot.com/max-ukropina-for-congress-2024/bf0ef0a9-11ee-489c-a57b-32f708bc5486?utm_medium=Email&utm_source=Ukropina&utm_campaign=Israel_Aid_113&utm_source=Max+for+OC+Supporters&utm_campaign=fa2c36367c-EMAIL_CAMPAIGN_2023_10_24_03_09_COPY_01&utm_medium=email&utm_term=0_-f436e3f042-%5BLIST_EMAIL_ID%5D)

It's the kind of conservative approach I'll fight for if I'm elected to Congress to represent Orange County.

[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/72757123/436289771/1638375543?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDYvMS84NTkxNCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIxZDEyNjIwOS05NTdhLWVlMTEtYjAwNC0wMDIyNDgzMmViNzMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=4KxN6n71LIRzhKhbdrxQv6PmgxE3IxSCJoM4W7p5x8U=&emci=845fddbc-7b7a-ee11-b004-00224832eb73&emdi=1d126209-957a-ee11-b004-00224832eb73&ceid=25681160) Can I tell you a story, Peter? I was born and grew up in a working-class family in Cheverly, Maryland. My mother was a public school teacher and my father was a salesman — both taught me what it means to work hard and help others. So when we fell on hard times and my dad lost our farm to bankruptcy, I vowed to do everything I could to provide for my family. **_[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/72757124/436289772/1638375543?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDYvMS84NTkxNCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIxZDEyNjIwOS05NTdhLWVlMTEtYjAwNC0wMDIyNDgzMmViNzMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=4KxN6n71LIRzhKhbdrxQv6PmgxE3IxSCJoM4W7p5x8U=&emci=845fddbc-7b7a-ee11-b004-00224832eb73&emdi=1d126209-957a-ee11-b004-00224832eb73&ceid=25681160)_** Who I am and where I come from is why I will always stand up for working families. That’s why I decided to run for Congress in 2018 and dedicate my career to being a champion for strengthening our middle class, creating good-paying jobs, and fighting for increased access to mental healthcare. clean_body: | Can I tell you a story, Peter? I was born and grew up in a working-class family in Cheverly, Maryland. My mother was a public school teacher and my father was a salesman — both taught me what it means to work hard and help others. So when we fell on hard times and my dad lost our farm to bankruptcy, I vowed to do everything I could to provide for my family. Who I am and where I come from is why I will always stand up for working families. That’s why I decided to run for Congress in 2018 and dedicate my career to being a champion for strengthening our middle class, creating good-paying jobs, and fighting for increased access to mental healthcare. Whether it was providing partner benefits and college tuition to employees at my company or fighting for issues that mattered most to you during my three years in Congress — I've always centered people in my work. [1]Justice Democrats

Peter,

Congress just passed a bill to give Israel $14.3 billion in military aid.

That’s $14.3 billion we apparently couldn’t afford to use here at home for
relieving student debt, providing universal healthcare, paying our
teachers a fair wage and improving our kids’ schools, or feeding the poor.

It’s $14.3 billion for more bombs that will undoubtedly end thousands of
innocent lives in Gaza, on top of the more than 9,000 people already
killed by Israel as they continue to target residential neighborhoods,
hospitals, and a massive refugee camp.

As hundreds of thousands of people across the United States continue to
organize, protest, and demand their elected officials support a ceasefire,
the majority of our government is enabling and funding genocide with our
tax dollars — but not the Squad.

Our bloc of progressive champions have loudly and proudly kept up the
fight for a ceasefire and an end to this ethnic cleansing. Despite the
vicious attacks against them, they’re not stopping and neither are we.

Justice Democrats is directly helping to turn the tide and elect diverse,

We’ve been racking our brains trying to think of a way to convince you to donate to Ruben Gallego’s U.S. Senate campaign in Arizona. We decided that the best way is to be honest with you.
So look. It would be one thing if Kari Lake was just a Republican.

It would be one thing if she accepted the insurrection at the Capitol on January 6th was one of the darkest days in the history of our country.

Peter,

It probably comes as no surprise to you that the last ten days have been a blur. Everything transpired so quickly that my own family wasn’t even able to make it to Washington, D.C. to watch me be sworn in as the 56th Speaker of the House.

My team and I – which has grown exponentially in the last week – really have been burning the midnight oil, working around the clock to ensure the people’s House remains OPEN FOR BUSINESS.

In the past week,

1. I’ve sifted through hundreds of resumes.
2. Met with the leaders from the Pentagon, the Senate, and the executive branch.
3. Sat for interviews with Sean Hannity and Larry Kudlow, among others.

name: Elizabeth Warren
subject: What exactly are “18th-century values”?
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Warren for Senate
body:
We’ve got to get this guy out of power.

| | | [ ](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/go/216?t=3&akid=132%2E4032634%2Eh8SvBm)
---
It seems like every day, we learn more about MAGA GOP House Speaker Mike Johnson’s extremist views. And we recently got a term that ties a bunch of them together in a neat (and horrifying) little bow. In 2013, in front of an anti-abortion rights group, Johnson said the Founding Fathers “told us that if we didn’t maintain those **18th-century values** , that the republic would not stand, and this is the condition we find ourselves in today.” Eighteenth-century values? Really? No wonder he’s...
* Blamed school shootings on an “amoral society” fostered in the 1960s and 1970s by “no-fault divorce laws,” “radical feminism,” and Roe v. Wade
* Said abortion providers should be sentenced to hard labor now that Roe is gone
* Called marriage equality a “dark harbinger of chaos and sexual anarchy that could doom even the strongest republic”
* Claimed same-sex relationships are “unnatural” and “harmful” and teamed up with an anti-LGBTQ+ group providing so-called “conversion therapy”
* Denied that the Constitution provides for the separation of church and state

This guy is way, way outside the mainstream. No wonder House Republicans picked him to represent them. But he clearly doesn’t belong anywhere near any position of authority. So we’ve got to use our power in our democracy to speak out — and to vote them out. [**Add your name to say you reject Speaker Mike Johnson’s extremism and you’re all-in to kick him and his fellow MAGA Republicans out of power.**](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/signup/ew-em-mikejohnson/?source=EMZ17H_GOP_E_20231103_V1S1&t=8&akid=132%2E4032634%2Eh8SvBm) | [**ADD YOUR NAME**](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/signup/ew-em-mikejohnson/?source=EMZ17H_GOP_E_20231103_V1S1&t=9&akid=132%2E4032634%2Eh8SvBm)

Elizabeth

Fellow American,

It probably comes as no surprise to you that the last ten days have been a blur. Everything transpired so quickly that my own family wasn’t even able to make it to Washington, D.C. to watch me be sworn in as the 56th Speaker of the House.

My team and I – which has grown exponentially in the last week – really have been burning the midnight oil, working around the clock to ensure the people’s House remains OPEN FOR BUSINESS.

In the past week,

1. I’ve sifted through hundreds of resumes.
2. Met with the leaders from the Pentagon, the Senate, and the executive branch.

subject: Rick Scott is a fraud

body:
I promise to always tell the truth about my story, my record, my beliefs, my state, and what I'll fight for
| | |
---
Team, these days, I keep finding myself saying this: _Rick Scott is a fraud._
He calls himself a public servant, but he's shown us time and time again that, in reality, _he only serves himself_. He's pushed an extreme agenda that hurts working families**** all while he saw his own net worth **_nearly triple_** as governor of Florida.
He claims to be an advocate for families and seniors, but **he wrote the plan to end Social Security and Medicare** — lifesaving programs that millions of Americans, including my mom, rely on.
**Rick Scott is a liar**. He pushed Donald Trump's Big Lie about the 2020 election, voted to overturn the 2020 election, falsely claimed that mail-in voting wasn't secure, and spread misinformation about Democrats like me.
As if that's not enough, **he actually oversaw the largest Medicare fraud scheme in our nation's HISTORY.** He made millions defrauding American taxpayers (a fortune that he later used to buy his way into the Senate).
**One of Rick Scott's latest frauds is trying to convince people that Floridians are all in on his extremist agenda.** That's a lie, through and through — in his last election, my opponent only won by 10,033 votes. The fact is, Floridians are ready for a change.
**I promise to always tell the truth about my story, my record, my beliefs, my state, and what I'll fight for in Washington. That's why my campaign is already polling 1 point ahead — and it's why I know we're going to end Rick Scott's decades-long grift next November. Fellow American,

It probably comes as no surprise to you that the last ten days have been a blur. Everything transpired so quickly that my own family wasn’t even able to make it to Washington, D.C. to watch me be sworn in as the 56th Speaker of the House.

My team and I – which has grown exponentially in the last week – really have been burning the midnight oil, working around the clock to ensure the people’s House remains OPEN FOR BUSINESS.

In the past week,

1. I’ve sifted through hundreds of resumes.
2. Met with the leaders from the Pentagon, the Senate, and the executive branch.
3. Sat for interviews with Sean Hannity and Larry Kudlow, among others.
4. Met with the campaign staff at the National Republican Congressional Committee to set finance goals for the upcoming year.

I’ve got to be honest with you – with so many competing priorities, [**it’s critical to have the _best_ team by my side.**](http://links.g4yamerica.com/u/click?_t=cc7dda5c2cc64061900678c88bd3a18a&_m=5b0f7357ebb144fa89effba6db3da93e&_e=0ge1SN9rRGlHAd6Dgs1UcwwoIRFy24DbruX0HP6asQX_Pb0Mldeg1NrjqHqKjxxPads8TA0zjLPNYKlPvpypwOgSM0ygIZVZovyE-WhawuG0NyYwTLrSXMq_qdCTLWIKm3iNqoRPtABy4wrTP90Tf42FObY0LnM4ZK1E3rUaQFqJexKayq9kjEv0qR_v_AQbLERBW0bTY15Y2xG6gVxnZMsk3wLUBwtoJhM972906aLnr4unXC-JVgCqJnxpQqc_IXkLI4v2-3t0bOSjY8UGrXobg3hZJ8IXEA8hL9lW46YJhcWaHBjryXXmOUC6EzlTCP5dZgldNK6UzIo5K20vhyYpqP8OrzRmEUBgmaQNDtBZFqhTz1sr_eVxD9JI4NXl7FjCz-7QiX44LdZzNE9sjA%3D%3D) I’m working to continue filling positions as fast as possible while fulfilling my duties outside of the Capitol.

You see, aside from my official duties as speaker, [**one of my new responsibilities is to be the chief fundraiser for the Republican Party.**](http://links.g4yamerica.com/u/click?_t=cc7dda5c2cc64061900678c88bd3a18a&_m=5b0f7357ebb144fa89effba6db3da93e&_e=0ge1SN9rRGlHAd6Dgs1UcwwoIRFy24DbruX0HP6asQX_Pb0Mldeg1NrjqHqKjxxPads8TA0zjLPNYKlPvpypwOgSM0ygIZVZovyE-WhawuG0NyYwTLrSXMq_qdCTLWIKm3iNqoRPtABy4wrTP90Tf42FObY0LnM4ZK1E3rUaQFqJexKayq9kjEv0qR_v_AQbLERBW0bTY15Y2xG6gVxnZMsk3wLUBwtoJhM972906aLnr4unXC-JVgCqJnxpQqc_iE73lPhFpkSLrI04L36J67kPkr4li9315ZjmUA-UthnEfnVChowHD8PyiZcTcqTW7ddrjboiGt8iUrEGohXZjViIpiS-lrF4nYNDPgyyCbg1F1dsxOeGlKLavhgIw2MAqv-IaE9unqTvF-gRnVhtNw%3D%3D) That means using this platform to raise money every single day of the year, so we have the necessary funds to defend our five-seat majority in next year’s election.

clean_body: It’s imperative you read this as soon as you see it. | | Fellow American, It probably comes as no surprise to you that the last ten days have been a blur. Everything transpired so quickly that my own family wasn’t even able to make it to Washington, D.C. to watch me be sworn in as the 56th Speaker of the House. My team and I – which has grown exponentially in the last week – really have been burning the midnight oil, working around the clock to ensure the people’s House remains OPEN FOR BUSINESS. In the past week, 1. I’ve sifted through hundreds of resumes. 2. Met with the leaders from the Pentagon, the Senate, and the executive branch. 3. Sat for interviews with Sean Hannity and Larry Kudlow, among others. 4. Met with the campaign staff at the National Republican Congressional Committee to set finance goals for the upcoming year. I’ve got to be honest with you – with so many competing priorities, I’m working to continue filling positions as fast as possible while fulfilling my duties outside of the Capitol. You see, aside from my official duties as speaker, That means using this platform to raise money every single day of the year, so we have the necessary funds to defend our five-seat majority in next year’s election. If we come up short, all bets are off. I have to get back to interviewing candidates to join my team, but I'll be checking in with my staff frequently over the next few days to see what progress we’ve made toward hitting this critical campaign goal.
